draft.title: Sound in film
card: Music
Music sets the mood of a scene. Slow, low notes that build can make a viewer feel tense, while bright, fast tunes can feel happy.
Sound effects
Sound effects are noises such as footsteps, a creaking door or a storm. They make a scene feel real and can warn the viewer or add fear.
Silence
When all sound stops, the viewer notices it. Silence can build suspense or make a moment feel shocking or sad.
Sound can work before anything happens on screen. A viewer may feel worried just from the sound of a scene.
draft.remember: Music, sound effects and silence all shape how a viewer feels.

a.q: In a film, a boy walks down a dark corridor. Low music slowly gets louder, but nothing has happened yet. What is the music mainly doing?
opts: Building suspense before anything happens
Showing that the corridor is a happy place
Making the scene feel calm and relaxed
Telling the viewer what the boy is thinking
a.why: Low music that builds can make a viewer feel tense, even before an event. It does not make a scene calm. It sets a mood and does not tell us what the boy thinks.
a.clue: Think about how slow, low music that grows louder makes you feel.

b.q: In a film, a loud storm rages, then all sound suddenly stops as Ava opens a door. What is the most likely effect of the sudden silence?
opts: It builds suspense and draws attention to the door
It shows that the storm has made her happy
It makes the scene feel more noisy and busy
It shows that sound effects are not needed
b.why: Silence after loud noise stands out, so the viewer pays close attention and may feel suspense. It does not make a scene noisy. The storm sounds earlier are sound effects, and the silence works because of the contrast with them.
b.clue: Notice how the sound changes from loud to nothing at all.

b.best: It builds suspense and draws attention to the door

card: Music

a.q: In a film, a boy walks down a dark corridor. Low music slowly gets louder with each step he takes. What is the music mainly doing?
opts: Making the viewer feel tense about what may come
Making the scene feel calm and peaceful
Telling the viewer exactly what the boy is thinking
Making the corridor seem cheerful and bright
a.why: Slow, low music that builds can make a viewer feel tense, even before any event on screen. It does not make a scene calm or cheerful. It sets a mood, but it does not tell us what the boy is thinking.
a.clue: Think about how slow, low music that grows louder makes you feel.

b.q: In a film, a loud storm rages, then all sound suddenly stops as Ava opens a door. What is the most likely effect of the sudden silence?
opts: It builds suspense about what is behind the door
It makes the scene feel calm and safe again
It makes the storm seem louder and closer
It tells the viewer exactly what Ava is thinking
b.why: Silence after loud noise stands out, so the viewer pays close attention and may feel suspense. It is tempting to think quiet means calm and safe, but sudden silence at a tense moment makes the viewer wait for something to happen.
b.clue: Notice how the sound changes from loud to nothing at all.
